$comment: Neutral shipped <sys/param.h> (Darwin/BSD), added by the SQLite-CLI-for-arm64-Darwin cycle. sqlite's os_unix.c needs exactly ONE thing from it — MAXPATHLEN, the bound of the AFP/conch path buffers — but a descriptor SHADOWS the real header TOTALLY (include_path_resolve.hpp:60-75, Descriptor → Source → NotFound), including on a NATIVE macOS host where the SDK header is what is used today via D-INCLUDE-ANGLE-SOURCE-FALLBACK, so what ships here has to be defensible for EVERY consumer of the name, not just for sqlite. ★ VALUES MEASURED against MacOSX26.4.sdk (extracted read-only at /tmp/apple_sdk_probe/MacOSX26.4.sdk/usr/include; nothing from the SDK is copied into this repo): sys/param.h:196 is `#define MAXPATHLEN PATH_MAX` and sys/syslimits.h:103 is `#define PATH_MAX 1024`, so MAXPATHLEN is 1024 — the SAME number that bounds f_mntonname / f_mntfromname in sys/mount.json's `struct statfs`, which is why that struct is 2168 bytes and not something else. sys/param.h:197 `#define MAXSYMLINKS 32` rides along because it is the other pathname-resolution limit the header owns and the pair is the closed, tiny domain a caller reaches for together — the same reasoning that makes sys/file.json ship all four LOCK_* rather than only the three sqlite uses. ★ PATH_MAX IS DELIBERATELY *NOT* RE-DECLARED HERE even though the real sys/param.h supplies it transitively (it #includes <sys/syslimits.h> at :93 and <limits.h> at :110). Its home is <limits.h>; cross-descriptor constants dedupe by NAME first-wins, so a second PATH_MAX row here would race limits.json for the binding and — the moment limits.json grows a per-format PATH_MAX (elf 4096 vs macho 1024, which is the honest per-format split) — could silently hand a macho build the wrong bound. Declining the duplicate keeps the fail-loud shape: a consumer that needs PATH_MAX includes <limits.h> and gets ONE answer. (MEASURED: no descriptor in shippedLibs declares PATH_MAX today.) The rest of the real header's surface — NCARGS/NGROUPS/NOFILE:99-101, MAXBSIZE, the roundup/powerof2 macros, and the transitive <sys/types.h>/<sys/signal.h>/<machine/param.h> re-includes — is NOT shipped: it has no consumer, and each row would be an unmeasured claim in a file that shadows the real thing. Tracked at D-FFI-DARWIN-SYS-PARAM-PARTIAL. ★ MAXPATHLEN ships as a `constants` row (the sys/stat.json S_IF* precedent) rather than a macro, and the probe for this cycle exercises it in ARRAY-BOUND position (`char buf[MAXPATHLEN];`) because that is how sqlite spells it — a constant that is not an integer constant expression would be a silent capability hole, so it is tested, not assumed. ★ NO `symbols` AND NO `library` KEY: this header declares no functions in C either, and DSS EAGER-IMPORTS every function a descriptor lists (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT — an unexported name breaks EVERY binary's LOAD), so the blast radius of including it is nil. Gated availableObjectFormats:[macho] — an elf/pe #include fails loud (the windows.json:5 [pe] precedent, inverted); glibc's own <sys/param.h> is a DIFFERENT header with different values and must not silently borrow these.
